phase_task.goal: The observability dashboard — the final phase, pure polish, strictly additive. A static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS bundle served by the gateway that renders KPI cards, a per-run timeline, and a filterable run table over data the platform ALREADY emits. It is an UNPRIVILEGED CONSUMER: it reads ONLY through the public API + structured logs/journal, with NO privileged access to the index, sandbox, or model. Its existence is itself evidence the API-only boundary holds — a full ops UI needs no backdoor. Must not touch or regress any core capability.

deliverables.d: Static bundle (vanilla HTML/CSS/JS — no framework, no build step, no browser storage): dark theme, KPI-card row + per-run timeline + filterable run table. Served by the gateway as a static asset route (e.g. GET /dashboard), NOT a new service and NOT a privileged path. No localStorage/sessionStorage; the dashboard holds no state the server doesn't expose — reopening it reconstructs everything from the API.

Reads ONLY existing public surfaces: the /v1 task status + events endpoints, /metrics, and the journal-as-trace (via an existing/thin read-only endpoint that is itself auth-scoped exactly like the rest of /v1 — a user sees only their own runs). It introduces NO endpoint that reaches the raw index, shells the sandbox, or calls the model. If a read-only aggregate endpoint is needed to feed KPIs, it must be auth-scoped per-user and expose only already-emitted metering/journal data — never internal state.

KPI cards from data already metered: tasks by terminal state (verified-success / gave-up / budget-exhausted), injections defended + secrets redacted (from the redaction/journal events), sandbox runs pass/fail, tokens + $ spent vs budget. Per-run timeline: the journal rendered as the plan→retrieve→edit→verify→repair state machine, each step with its tokens/bytes/sandbox-seconds and result. Filterable run table: task_id, terminal state, tokens, $, wall-time, verified?.

make logs opens the dashboard: snapshot by default; LIVE=1 auto-refreshes by polling /metrics + events. Thin delegate to agentctl/compose per the Makefile-as-interface rule. Still tails raw structured logs as before.

Auth + isolation preserved: the dashboard is subject to the same auth as any consumer — it cannot show another user's runs. A dashboard request with no/bad key gets the same 401; run/journal data is user-scoped (NotFound for non-owner), identical to Phase 6. Assert this.

Zero regression: the core is untouched except the static-asset route + any thin auth-scoped read endpoint. Full existing suite (205 with images) stays green; make up still boots one-command keyless on the Python default.

phase_task.oracle: Via make test + a documented manual open: (1) the dashboard renders correctly for real runs (happy, resume, budget-exhausted, injection-defense) using ONLY public endpoints — assert the served page + its data endpoints are all public/auth-scoped, none privileged; (2) grep/inventory the dashboard's data calls and assert ZERO calls to any index/sandbox/model internal — it reaches nothing a consumer couldn't; (3) AUTH/ISOLATION — a dashboard data request with no/bad key -> 401; user A cannot see user B's runs (NotFound), same as Phase 6; (4) NO browser storage — assert the bundle contains no localStorage/sessionStorage usage (stateless by construction); (5) make logs opens snapshot; make logs LIVE=1 polls and refreshes; (6) zero regression — full suite green on Python default, make up boots one-command. Each clause by actual mechanism, no proxies.
phase_task.docs: DESIGN.md operability section: the dashboard as an UNPRIVILEGED CONSUMER — reads only public API + logs/journal, no backdoor — and why that is itself evidence the API-only boundary holds. Note the deliberate no-browser-storage choice (distinct from a personal tracker) and why a multi-user ops surface must be stateless/server-fed. Update SLOs/operability with what the dashboard surfaces. If a thin read-only aggregate endpoint was added, document it in the API/route inventory (§10) with its auth scope, and update the API-only boundary claim + its proving test to include the new route.
phase_task.stop: This is the final build phase — after it, only git-history reconstruction, the walkthrough, and any revisited judgment calls remain. Report: the dashboard's exact data sources (every endpoint it calls) and proof each is public/auth-scoped and none privileged; the auth/isolation result (401 + cross-user NotFound); the no-browser-storage assertion; the make logs snapshot + LIVE behavior; confirmation of zero regression (full suite green on Python default + make up one-command); and the updated route inventory if any endpoint was added. State anything cut.
